fixed.explanation: validate_metadata passed dtype_equal=True to array_equivalent even though the new and stored categories can have different dtypes (int64 vs float64). That flag skips the dtype check and sends the arrays to a typed Cython routine, which raises a buffer dtype mismatch. Without the flag, array_equivalent compares dtypes itself and returns False, so the intended "different categories" ValueError is raised.

query.intent: When appending to a PyTables table-format store, the code validates that new categorical categories match the stored ones (in the categorical/Categorical column handling in pandas/io/pytables.py, e.g. validate_col / update_info / _maybe_convert / metadata comparison). It compares categories arrays of different dtypes with a Cython/hashtable-based routine (e.g. array_equivalent or Index.equals/isin) that raises a buffer dtype mismatch instead of returning False, so the intended "cannot append categories differ" ValueError is not raised.
